No 2026 quarter-end covenant ratio is printed, and the net bank leverage of 3.8x, 3.7x and 3.8x in the releases has no printed definition.; Headroom at the latest date cannot be stated, and net bank leverage cannot be reconciled to the covenant measure.; Supply the compliance certificate or the covenant definitions.; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 1

facts.label: Financial interpretation
facts.text: Leverage has improved because debt fell while earnings rose. Total debt at carrying value fell from USD 5,130.2 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 4,722 million at 2026-09-30, mainly because revolver borrowings were repaid from operating cash flow of USD 660 million in nine months after USD 176 million of capital expenditure and USD 44 million of buybacks, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,063.2 million to USD 1,157.2 million. The gain rests on restrained spending: capital project expenditure was USD 119 million against USD 172 million a year earlier, and buybacks were USD 44 million against USD 396 million, so a return to the pace of 2025 would slow deleveraging. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 76–79; calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C10

facts.text: Cash interest cover improved to 4.22x from 3.61x because cash interest paid fell to USD 274.5 million on a last-twelve-months basis from USD 294.5 million as the revolver was paid down. facts.text: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was unrestricted cash of USD 167 million plus about USD 1,111 million of undrawn revolver capacity after USD 10 million of letters of credit; restricted cash of USD 92 million is excluded. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the 2026 record: buybacks fell to USD 44 million in nine months from USD 396 million a year earlier, revolver borrowings fell by USD 578 million, the bank facilities were extended to September 2031, and the dividend has risen for sixteen consecutive years and is small against free cash flow. A diversified base of ten owned casinos, many racing and historical racing venues and a flagship event also limits single-asset risk. The view would turn adverse if buybacks under the new USD 750 million authorization were funded with revolver draws, if the USD 85 million Preakness purchase or the Rockingham investment were financed by borrowing without offsetting repayment, or if the proxy statement or financing documents showed a concentrated holder or loose restricted-payment baskets. It would improve if covenant ratios and indenture terms confirmed tight limits on distributions. facts.label: T2D.9 Sponsor risk assessment
facts.text: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a constructive view is that leverage of 4.08x reported EBITDA is still material for a business whose earnings fall in one quarter, that Adjusted EBITDA flatters leverage by including the share of equity investees' EBITDA whose cash reaches the company only as distributions, and that the interest rate exposure rises after the revolver-funded redemption of the 2027 notes. A further weakness is that covenant ratios for 2026 and the definition of the quoted net bank leverage of 3.8x are not printed. The view would weaken if buybacks under the new USD 750 million authorization are funded with revolver draws, if the 2028 notes are not refinanced before the test date, if Virginia historical racing earnings keep falling after the new tax, or if the post-redemption revolver balance shows liquidity well below the USD 1,278 million seen at 2026-09-30. It would strengthen if the next quarterly report shows revolver repayment continuing and covenant ratios with wide headroom. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A supported downside begins with a poor Kentucky Derby week or a regulatory or tax change in Kentucky or Virginia, which would first cut second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA, the quarter that supplies 37.42% of the year. Lower earnings would raise leverage from 4.08x and reduce free cash flow, and with the revolver already used for the 2027 redemption and a buyback authorization of USD 750 million, management levers are to cut buybacks and project capital, which are discretionary. Liquidity of USD 1,278 million at 2026-09-30 and no bank maturity before 2031 mean resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress unless the 2028 notes are not refinanced by the springing test date, when about USD 1,148 million of bank debt could be pulled forward. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Churchill Downs presents an adequate business profile supported by regional diversification, regulated venues and a flagship event, but credit quality is constrained by event and regulatory concentration, committed project capital and shareholder-return capacity. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is 45.79% of reported EBITDA, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on cash flow, revolver availability and the refinancing of the USD 700 million notes due in January 2028. The primary downside path is a weak Kentucky Derby quarter or a Virginia or Kentucky rule change that lifts leverage while buybacks and projects continue. Further analysis would require the post-redemption revolver balance, 2026 covenant ratios and the executed financing documents. Top risk: refinancing the January 2028 notes before the bank facilities' springing maturity test. ## Request

Churchill Downs Inc (registrant Churchill Downs Incorporated, Nasdaq: CHDN) as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is whether the seven supplied filings and releases support the requested financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit work. It also records what each wider capability lacks.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support the financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit work on Churchill Downs Inc through the third quarter of 2026, but covenant, legal-priority, ratings and market-implied work lack executed documents, rating reports and quotes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 1

The last printed covenant ratios are at the end of 2025, and the releases quote a net bank leverage measure whose definition is not printed. Two note maturity dates differ between the annual report and the quarterly reports, and the closing of the Preakness rights purchase is not stated after the first quarter. Each is logged under the gaps.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Total debt to reported EBITDA fell to 4.08x at 2026-09-30 from 4.83x at 2025-12-31 as debt was repaid and earnings grew, which strengthens creditors, but the October 2026 redemption of the 2027 notes with revolver borrowings moves fixed-rate debt onto floating-rate debt.

### Financial interpretation

Leverage has improved because debt fell while earnings rose. Total debt at carrying value fell from USD 5,130.2 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 4,722 million at 2026-09-30, mainly because revolver borrowings were repaid from operating cash flow of USD 660 million in nine months after USD 176 million of capital expenditure and USD 44 million of buybacks, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,063.2 million to USD 1,157.2 million. The gain rests on restrained spending: capital project expenditure was USD 119 million against USD 172 million a year earlier, and buybacks were USD 44 million against USD 396 million, so a return to the pace of 2025 would slow deleveraging.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 76–79; calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C10

Cash interest cover improved to 4.22x from 3.61x because cash interest paid fell to USD 274.5 million on a last-twelve-months basis from USD 294.5 million as the revolver was paid down. That benefit is exposed to the October 2026 redemption of the USD 600 million 5.50% 2027 notes with revolver borrowings: the weighted average rate on the Credit Agreement was 5.48% at 2026-09-30, so the fixed coupon is replaced by a floating rate of similar cost, and the issuer states that a one-percentage-point rise in the reference rate would cost USD 12 million on USD 1.6 billion of variable debt before this redemption. The filing prints no post-redemption variable balance, so the new sensitivity is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C05

Cash generation is of reasonable quality but depends on the equity investees. Distributions from unconsolidated affiliates were USD 106 million in nine months 2026 against equity income of USD 115 million, so cash receipts track reported earnings, and free cash flow after total capital expenditure was USD 484 million against USD 449 million in nine months 2025. Cash taxes paid rose to USD 65 million from USD 17 million, which absorbed part of the interest saving. Contract liabilities of USD 60 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 80 million at 2025-12-31 relate largely to advance Kentucky Derby receipts; they are working-capital float that unwinds after the spring and is not debt, but it flatters March quarter-end net debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C10

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was unrestricted cash of USD 167 million plus about USD 1,111 million of undrawn revolver capacity after USD 10 million of letters of credit; restricted cash of USD 92 million is excluded. The strongest counter to the improving picture is the structure of the bank facilities: they were extended to September 2031 but carry a springing maturity if the notes maturing earlier are not refinanced at least 91 days before they mature, so the USD 700 million 2028 notes are the first practical test for the revolver and term loan A. What would change this view is a revolver draw after the October redemption that is larger than the principal redeemed, a resumption of large buybacks under the new USD 750 million authorization, or covenant ratios, which are not printed for 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C07

Two definition risks limit comparison with the issuer's own measures. The company prints Adjusted EBITDA only, which includes its share of the EBITDA of equity investees whose cash arrives as distributions, so leverage on Adjusted EBITDA (3.79x total) looks better than on reported EBITDA (4.08x), and the quarterly releases quote net bank leverage of 3.8x without a definition. The quarterly debt table labelled Net debt is the non-current debt balance before cash, not net debt in the usual sense.

The FY2024 net change in cash is not supplied because it includes USD 1.0 million of discontinued operations cash flow outside the three activity totals.

- Low: Cost of sales and gross profit are not presented (costs are shown by segment), gross interest expense and interest income are not separately stated, and maintenance against growth capital expenditure is available only as capital maintenance and capital project lines; coverage uses net interest expense and cash interest paid.

- Low: Lease and other obligations carried outside the debt lines (operating lease minimum rent of USD 52 million, financing obligations of USD 31 million and other contractual obligations of USD 9 million at 2026-09-30) are not added to Total Debt; no pension or retiree medical obligation was found in the documents read.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48

## Findings
### Bottom line

Churchill Downs is a listed, widely held company with no sponsor or controlling owner identified in the documents, so creditors rely on management's capital allocation, which turned from heavy buybacks in 2025 to debt repayment in 2026, rather than on owner support.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 133–134; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C03

Earnings are concentrated in the Kentucky Derby quarter and in historical racing machine venues, and 14.78% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA is equity income from two unconsolidated casinos whose cash arrives as distributions. Sponsor and governance risk is assessed as medium: shareholder returns absorbed 92.67% of free cash flow in FY2025 but have been restrained in 2026, and no creditor-adverse action is documented, while ownership percentages and the financing documents were not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04
### Key findings

The business is a three-segment racing, wagering and casino operator led by Live and Historical Racing, which was 47.67% of FY2025 net revenue and 49.10% of FY2025 segment Adjusted EBITDA, with Gaming at 35.64% of revenue and 37.23% of segment earnings. That mix ties earnings to one flagship event and to historical racing machine regulation in Kentucky and Virginia, so a regulatory or competitive change in a few states moves consolidated cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; calculation C01

Earnings are strongly seasonal: the second quarter, which holds the Kentucky Derby, produced USD 451 million of USD 1,205.3 million of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, or 37.42%, so any single quarter-end balance sheet or leverage figure misrepresents the year and leverage is best read on a last-twelve-months basis.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C02

Equity investees are a material but cash-lagged part of earnings: Gaming segment Adjusted EBITDA includes USD 178.1 million of equity income from the 61.3% interest in Midwest Gaming (Rivers Des Plaines) and the 50% interest in Miami Valley Gaming, equal to 14.78% of consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, while distributions received in FY2025 were USD 116.0 million against equity income of USD 139.4 million. Creditors reach that cash only as distributions, and the investees' own debt is outside the consolidated debt table.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77–79; calculation C04

Capital allocation is the main ownership-related risk. In FY2025 dividends of USD 30.8 million and buybacks of USD 427.8 million were 92.67% of free cash flow of USD 494.9 million, revolver borrowings rose by USD 279.5 million and the company bought 90% of Casino Salem for USD 180 million; in nine months 2026 dividends and buybacks were USD 75 million against free cash flow of USD 484 million and revolver borrowings fell by USD 578 million. Restraint in 2026 lowers risk now, but the new USD 750 million repurchase authorization shows that capacity to resume larger returns exists.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78–79; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C03; calculation C05

Expansion is debt-funded before it earns: Casino Salem is being redeveloped as Rockingham Grand Casino with USD 180 million to USD 200 million of planned investment for a mid-2027 opening, a USD 280 million to USD 300 million building at Churchill Downs Racetrack is planned by the 2028 Kentucky Derby, and a USD 85 million Preakness purchase was agreed in April 2026 with its closing not stated. These commitments compete with debt reduction in 2027 and 2028.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-03-31_chdn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 20

No sponsor, equity support, drop-down, priming or amendment-and-extension behaviour against creditors is documented. The September 2026 bank amendment extended maturities, and the largest related-party style transaction, the repurchase of one million shares from an affiliate of The Duchossois Group in 2023, was approved by the board separately and funded with cash and credit facility borrowings. Legal capacity for restricted payments and debt cannot be tested because no executed financing documents were supplied.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the 2026 record: buybacks fell to USD 44 million in nine months from USD 396 million a year earlier, revolver borrowings fell by USD 578 million, the bank facilities were extended to September 2031, and the dividend has risen for sixteen consecutive years and is small against free cash flow. A diversified base of ten owned casinos, many racing and historical racing venues and a flagship event also limits single-asset risk. The view would turn adverse if buybacks under the new USD 750 million authorization were funded with revolver draws, if the USD 85 million Preakness purchase or the Rockingham investment were financed by borrowing without offsetting repayment, or if the proxy statement or financing documents showed a concentrated holder or loose restricted-payment baskets. It would improve if covenant ratios and indenture terms confirmed tight limits on distributions.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation C03
### Limitations

- Ownership percentages, director independence and compensation are not established because the proxy statement was not supplied, so the finding that no controlling owner exists rests on a holder count and on the absence of any sponsor in the documents, and a concentrated holder would raise the governance risk level.

- No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, buybacks, debt and asset transfers is not tested and the medium risk level cannot be lowered on capacity grounds.

- Segment revenue shares use external revenue while segment Adjusted EBITDA is built on segment revenue that includes intercompany amounts, so the revenue and earnings shares are indicative and not directly comparable.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; calculation C01
- The closing of the Preakness purchase is not stated after April 2026, so its funding and cash effect are not in the capital allocation conclusion.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_chdn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 20

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Casino Salem was the last completed acquisition: on August 27, 2025 the company bought 90% of the equity of Casino Salem for a base price of USD 180 million, recorded as an asset acquisition with a USD 197 million gaming rights intangible, and funded it with revolver borrowings. The company then redevelops the site as Rockingham Grand Casino, with USD 180 million to USD 200 million planned and a mid-2027 opening.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1

The financing changed materially in September and October 2026. On September 25, 2026 the company closed the eighth amendment to the Credit Agreement, extending the revolver and term loan A to September 2031 with a springing maturity, and entered a new USD 500 million term loan B due 2033 at 99.875% priced at SOFR plus 175 basis points; proceeds repaid the 2028 term loan B and part of the revolver. A conditional redemption notice for the 2027 notes was issued on September 18, 2026 and the notes were redeemed on October 19, 2026 with revolver borrowings, so the debt table at 2026-09-30 still shows them.

Other transactions are the re-acquisition on August 3, 2026 of the 49% of United Tote held by NYRA (with NYRA's tote services agreement extended through 2035), the Preakness Stakes and Black-Eyed Susan Stakes intellectual property purchase for USD 85 million agreed on April 21, 2026 and not reported as closed, and the new USD 750 million repurchase program approved on October 27, 2026, which includes USD 306 million left under the earlier program.

spans.text: ## Request

Churchill Downs Inc as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the fundamental credit view: business and operating model, cash flow durability, financial profile, refinancing position, the primary downside path and monitoring triggers. It uses the supplied financial foundation and business and governance analyses and makes no covenant, legal-priority, recovery or relative-value conclusion.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Churchill Downs is a cash-generative, seasonal racing and casino operator whose leverage has fallen to 4.08x reported EBITDA, which supports creditors, but the bank facilities' springing maturity makes the notes due in January 2028 the key refinancing test.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C01; calculation C06

Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 484 million in nine months 2026, against shareholder payouts of USD 75 million, but payouts took 92.67% of free cash flow in FY2025, so the view depends on continued restraint. Covenant headroom, legal priority and the post-redemption revolver balance are not established, and quarter-end balances are not representative because the Kentucky Derby falls in the second quarter.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C03; calculation C04
### Key findings

Business quality is adequate and event-concentrated: Live and Historical Racing earns the largest share of segment profit, and the second quarter produced 37.42% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, so one flagship event and historical racing machine rules in Kentucky and Virginia carry a large part of the debt service capacity. The 16 historical racing venues, ten owned casinos and online wagering give geographic spread that single-asset operators lack.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C04

Cash flow conversion is solid: last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 529.9 million is 45.79% of reported EBITDA, with capital expenditure well below the FY2025 level, but conversion in 2026 benefits from lower project capital and the planned Rockingham and First Turn projects will absorb cash again.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02

Leverage is improving but still material: total debt is 4.08x and net debt 3.94x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, down from 4.83x at 2025-12-31, and cash interest cover is 4.22x against 3.61x. On the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back its share of equity investees' EBITDA, total leverage is 3.79x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

Liquidity is adequate: unrestricted cash of USD 167 million and about USD 1,111 million of undrawn revolver capacity give 1.83x cover of the USD 700 million notes due in January 2028, but the October 2026 redemption of the 2027 notes was funded from the revolver, so the post-redemption position is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C05

Refinancing depends on the 2028 notes: the revolver and term loan A, USD 1,148 million at 2026-09-30, mature in September 2031 only if notes maturing earlier are refinanced at least 91 days before maturity, a test that falls on 2027-10-16 for the 2028 notes; the longest-dated debt is the USD 500 million term loan B due 2033. No large note maturity falls before January 2028 after the 2027 redemption.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C06

Financial policy is the main judgement: dividends are small, but FY2025 buybacks and dividends took 92.67% of free cash flow with revolver borrowings rising, while payouts were 15.50% in nine months 2026. Sponsor and governance risk is medium, with no sponsor, no documented creditor-adverse action and legal capacity not testable.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C03
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a constructive view is that leverage of 4.08x reported EBITDA is still material for a business whose earnings fall in one quarter, that Adjusted EBITDA flatters leverage by including the share of equity investees' EBITDA whose cash reaches the company only as distributions, and that the interest rate exposure rises after the revolver-funded redemption of the 2027 notes. A further weakness is that covenant ratios for 2026 and the definition of the quoted net bank leverage of 3.8x are not printed. The view would weaken if buybacks under the new USD 750 million authorization are funded with revolver draws, if the 2028 notes are not refinanced before the test date, if Virginia historical racing earnings keep falling after the new tax, or if the post-redemption revolver balance shows liquidity well below the USD 1,278 million seen at 2026-09-30. It would strengthen if the next quarterly report shows revolver repayment continuing and covenant ratios with wide headroom.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; calculation C05; calculation C07
### Limitations

- The post-redemption revolver balance, the amount drawn on 2026-10-19 and the resulting undrawn capacity are not printed, so the liquidity and refinancing conclusions are stated at 2026-09-30 and could be weaker after the redemption.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

- Covenant levels are printed only for 2025-12-31 and no financing document was supplied, so the leverage view is not tied to covenant headroom and a covenant-driven default path cannot be ruled in or out.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 69

- The financial profile is qualitative where inputs are missing: no operating series such as handle, attendance or venue-level results was extracted, so revenue durability rests on segment totals and one flagship event.
- Rating agency views, peer leverage and market prices were not supplied, so the view is not benchmarked against the sector and says nothing about relative value.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: the business is spread across racing, wagering and casino earnings. Evidence is that Live and Historical Racing, Wagering Services and Solutions and Gaming produced USD 637.0 million, USD 177.3 million and USD 483.0 million of FY2025 segment Adjusted EBITDA, so no single segment exceeds half of the total. The mechanism is that a shock to one segment is cushioned by the others, which supports debt service capacity and refinancing confidence.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; calculation C04

Strength: cash generation and deleveraging. Evidence is last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 529.9 million and a fall in total debt to reported EBITDA from 4.83x to 4.08x in nine months. The mechanism is that operating cash flow after capital expenditure was applied to the revolver, which shortens the time to a lower leverage level and widens the cushion for the 2028 refinancing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02

Strength: extended bank maturities and ample liquidity at the balance sheet date. Evidence is the September 2026 amendment moving the revolver and term loan A to September 2031 and USD 1,278 million of cash and undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-09-30. The mechanism is that no bank maturity falls before 2031 unless the springing test is triggered, so near-term refinancing pressure is limited.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05

Weakness: earnings concentration in the Kentucky Derby quarter and in historical racing rules. Evidence is 37.42% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA in the second quarter and a USD 10 million decrease in Central Virginia Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026 from competition and a new tax. The mechanism is that a weather, regulatory or tax event concentrates loss in a few states and one quarter, so leverage and liquidity can move sharply.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C04

Weakness: shareholder returns and growth projects compete with deleveraging. Evidence is FY2025 payouts of 92.67% of free cash flow, a USD 750 million repurchase authorization and USD 460 million to USD 500 million of announced Rockingham and First Turn investment. The mechanism is that debt-funded returns or projects would lift leverage again, which leaves recovery to depend on management restraint.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C03

Weakness: floating-rate exposure and a bank facility tied to the notes. Evidence is the revolver-funded redemption of the USD 600 million 2027 notes and a springing maturity linked to the 2028 notes. The mechanism is that fixed coupon debt is replaced by debt that reprices and that bank maturities can be pulled forward, which raises cash interest and refinancing risk if markets are shut.

Module status: Ready with Limitations.
### Company description

Churchill Downs operates the Kentucky Derby venue, 16 historical racing venues in Kentucky and Virginia, online horse wagering and wagering technology, and ten wholly owned and two equity-investee casinos. Revenue is largely transactional and discretionary, tied to attendance, wagering and gaming volume, so cash flow visibility is lower than for contracted businesses, but it is regulated, licensed and spread across many venues, which supports debt service in ordinary conditions and refinancing confidence.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–14
### Ownership and group structure

The company is publicly listed with about 1,940 holders of record and no sponsor or controlling owner identified, so there is no sponsor equity cure and no sponsor-driven recapitalisation in the documents, and creditors depend on board and management financial policy. Casino Salem is 90% owned, two casinos are equity-accounted investees, and the subsidiary guarantors and collateral terms are not printed, so structurally senior claims and restricted group boundaries are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue growth is slowing: net revenue rose 7.01% in FY2025 and 3.50% in nine months 2026, with volume from new venues in Kentucky and Virginia offset by competition and tax in Central Virginia. Pricing power is limited because wagering is a pass-through of pari-mutuel commissions and gaming taxes are set by states, so revenue is cyclical, regulated and exposed to substitution from other gaming and betting, and growth depends on new venues rather than price.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14; calculation C08
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins have been stable: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 42.39% in FY2024, 41.19% in FY2025 and 42.67% in nine months 2026 against 42.39% a year earlier. Pari-mutuel taxes and purses of USD 349.4 million against Live and Historical Racing segment revenue of USD 1,442.4 million and gaming taxes are variable with volume, which protects margin in a downturn, while salaries, maintenance and venue costs are fixed and create operating leverage when attendance falls.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; calculation C08
### Capital intensity and cash flow conversion

EBITDA converts to free cash flow at 45.79% on a last-twelve-months basis, helped by distributions from investees and by project capital falling to USD 119 million in nine months 2026 from USD 172 million. Capital expenditure is largely discretionary until committed, but the Rockingham investment of USD 180 million to USD 200 million and the First Turn building of USD 280 million to USD 300 million are committed, and deferred revenue from advance Derby receipts unwinds through the year, so cash conversion is seasonal.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C02
### Market forces

Competition from other casinos, sports betting and other states' historical racing venues is the main force, buyer power is low because customers are individual patrons, and licensing and tax barriers limit new entrants but are set by states and can change. Macro, regulatory and tax factors are credit drivers only through gaming and pari-mutuel regulation, which the monitoring triggers cover; other macro and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the provided materials.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months tailwinds are the full-year effect of new Kentucky and Virginia venues, lower interest cost from debt repayment and extended bank maturities; headwinds are the Virginia tax and competition effect, the revolver-funded note redemption, committed project capital and the January 2028 notes. Over three to five years the opening of Rockingham and the First Turn building add earnings capacity only if funded without lifting leverage, and the sector remains exposed to state policy.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16
### Downside scenario

A supported downside begins with a poor Kentucky Derby week or a regulatory or tax change in Kentucky or Virginia, which would first cut second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA, the quarter that supplies 37.42% of the year. Lower earnings would raise leverage from 4.08x and reduce free cash flow, and with the revolver already used for the 2027 redemption and a buyback authorization of USD 750 million, management levers are to cut buybacks and project capital, which are discretionary. Liquidity of USD 1,278 million at 2026-09-30 and no bank maturity before 2031 mean resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress unless the 2028 notes are not refinanced by the springing test date, when about USD 1,148 million of bank debt could be pulled forward.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06
### Overall credit view

Overall, Churchill Downs presents an adequate business profile supported by regional diversification, regulated venues and a flagship event, but credit quality is constrained by event and regulatory concentration, committed project capital and shareholder-return capacity. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is 45.79% of reported EBITDA, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on cash flow, revolver availability and the refinancing of the USD 700 million notes due in January 2028. The primary downside path is a weak Kentucky Derby quarter or a Virginia or Kentucky rule change that lifts leverage while buybacks and projects continue. Further analysis would require the post-redemption revolver balance, 2026 covenant ratios and the executed financing documents. Top risk: refinancing the January 2028 notes before the bank facilities' springing maturity test.
